routes.description: Establish that theism offers a better overall explanation by supplying a non-causal ground for contingent reality, a principled ultimate explanatory terminus, and an epistemically coherent account of religious experience and diversity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the theistic resources jointly provide material explanatory advantages over naturalistic alternatives while meeting challenges concerning brute necessity, experiential unreliability, divine communication, and religious disagreement.

motionBridge.description: Show that theism's combined treatment of contingent reality and religious experience makes it the better overall explanation relative to naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Require a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation of the contingent total causal history and identify divine free grounding as the relevant resource.
Provide a principled ultimate terminus whose essence entails existence and explain why a theistic candidate has comparative explanatory relevance.
Justify giving context-sensitive evidential weight to religious experience, testimony, and cultivated religious practices.
Account for ambiguity and religious diversity without requiring that divine communication chiefly produce uniform and detailed theology.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify grounding as the relation by which divine creative activity could unify and explain created causal reality.
Distinguish degrees of experiential and testimonial reliability while preserving qualified trust amid disagreement.

routes.description: Establish that naturalism can match or exceed theism's explanatory coverage without adding God by offering naturalistic foundations for contingent history and explaining religious phenomena through calibrated cognition, social processes, and nonintentional causes.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts cover the principal explanatory domains without a uniquely theistic resource and if the proposed theistic stopping points and experiential expectations do not establish an overall comparative advantage.

motionBridge.description: Show that adding God does not improve the overall explanation once naturalistic alternatives and the comparative costs of theistic explanations are included.

centralBridges.description: Supply a naturalistic structure in which necessary initial reality and indeterministic evolution explain the occurrence of a contingent history.
Require equal scrutiny of naturalistic and theistic ultimate necessities and deny an asymmetry based only on naming a developed divine essence.
Explain why religious experience must be calibrated for ordinary unreliability, cognitive mechanisms, and the relevant comparison class.
Relate ambiguity, unsuccessful visionaries, and enduring religious diversity to the expectations of intentional divine communication and naturalistic causation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Compare explanatory coverage and simplicity across complete worldviews without double-counting a disputed explanatory deficiency.
Preserve live naturalistic ultimate candidates where present knowledge of cosmic origins does not determine their essential structure.

sections.title: Standards for Comparing Complete Worldviews
sections.rationale: This issue fixes how explanatory coverage, simplicity, uncertainty, and reasonable disagreement bear on the motion, and therefore governs how the more specific causal and experiential disputes contribute to an overall comparison.

sections.title: Grounding and the Explanation of Contingent Causal History
sections.rationale: The debate's principal metaphysical clash concerns whether contingent causal history requires a non-causal, non-necessitating ground or can be explained through necessary natural conditions with indeterministic evolution.

sections.title: Necessary Existence and Explanatory Termination
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether theism supplies a principled ultimate explanatory terminus unavailable to naturalism, or whether divine and natural foundations face symmetrical demands concerning necessity, essence, and bruteness.

sections.title: Epistemic Weight and Naturalistic Calibration of Religious Experience
sections.rationale: Religious experience is a distinct proposed source of comparative support whose force depends on default trust, testimonial and first-person justification, learned practices, cognitive mechanisms, and calibrated unreliability.

sections.title: Divine Communication, Visionaries, and Religious Diversity
sections.rationale: The distribution, ambiguity, and durability of divergent traditions test whether religious phenomena fit intentional divine relationship or nonintentional natural and sociological processes within the competing worldviews.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Naturalists can construct a comparably explanatory worldview without adding God, regardless of the broad shape of causal reality.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly gives Graham Oppy the first opening statement, and the uninterrupted first-person exposition is his.

response.rationale: This constructive move states the con side's overall comparative thesis and establishes the intended worldview-comparison framework.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly establishes the governing comparative claim but develops its support mainly through later moves.

precisionFindings.rationale: The comparative thesis is recoverable, though the phrase covering any broad causal shape leaves its exact range only implicitly bounded.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move advances a programmatic possibility of naturalistic comparability rather than claiming that every detailed naturalism is established.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The program is internally consistent, but the bridge from broad causal possibilities to comparable total explanation remains compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The source supplies a methodological proposal but not yet representative domain-by-domain support or a serious cost comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The claim directly advances the con motion bridge by asserting explanatory comparability without adding God.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move primarily presents its own comparative program and does not materially characterize a developed opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy says that, regardless of the broad shape assigned to causal reality, a naturalist can construct an explanatory worldview.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Comparing explanatory coverage and theoretical simplicity requires judgment and can permit reasonable disagreement rather than yielding an algorithmically decisive result.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator proposes a characterization, after which Oppy qualifies it in a sustained first-person response.

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies a subsidiary methodological qualification concerning judgment, simplicity, and reasonable disagreement.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly and explicitly defines how comparative conclusions should be understood and qualified.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move explicitly limits the comparison to judgment capable of supporting more than one reasonable conclusion.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Its modest assertion that alternative overall judgments can be reasonable is expressly qualified and proportionate to the stated support.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between reasoned comparative judgment and algorithmic decisiveness is explicit, consistent, and appropriately limited.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conclusion is supported by the role assigned to judgment, though no detailed account of virtue aggregation is supplied.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It materially supports the con subsidiary worldview-method bridge but does not itself decide overall explanatory comparability.

representationalCharity.rationale: No developed opposing argument is assessed; the move instead acknowledges the possibility of reasonable alternative judgment.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy expressly calls the comparison a matter of judgment and concedes that an alternative overall judgment can reasonably be made.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Arguments can identify genuine considerations favoring theism or naturalism even when there is no agreed algorithm for uniquely balancing all worldview virtues.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator directly invites Kenny Pearce to present his case, and Pearce begins with an explicit statement of agreement and disagreement.

components.text: Whether reasonable disagreement leaves arguments able to identify genuine comparative considerations.

response.rationale: Pearce accepts the absence of a uniquely determining algorithm while directly preserving a substantive role for arguments identifying comparative advantages.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it expressly contacts the decisive methodological implication and gives a clear qualified answer.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move clearly distinguishes identifying favoring reasons from compelling one uniquely correct aggregate worldview judgment.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The limited claim that arguments retain a comparative role fits the concession that balancing all considerations is not algorithmic.

charity.alternative: Reasonable disagreement may mean no argument can establish a uniquely mandatory total-worldview judgment.
charity.decisiveQualification: Arguments may still identify genuine local advantages without uniquely aggregating every theoretical virtue.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between identifying reasons and uniquely aggregating them is explicit and resolves the apparent tension with reasonable disagreement.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual distinction supports the conclusion, though no detailed examples of the promised comparative advantages appear in this span.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The reply directly attacks a possible overextension of the con subsidiary worldview-method claim.

representationalCharity.rationale: Pearce accepts the strongest methodological qualification and accurately limits his contrary conclusion to identifying favoring reasons.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce agrees that disagreement need not make one party simply wrong, then says arguments can call attention to reasons favoring either side.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: The contingent total causal history requires a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation, for which divine free grounding supplies a resource not identified within science-oriented naturalism.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce identifies this as his contingency argument and develops it continuously, with only brief clarifying interventions from the moderator.

components.text: Whether naturalism can explain contingent causal history without a distinct non-causal, non-necessitating resource.

response.rationale: The move directly identifies an alleged explanatory deficit in naturalism and proposes divine free grounding as the contrasting theistic resource.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the key explanatory-coverage claim, although the necessity of the demanded explanation remains underargued.

precisionFindings.rationale: The needed explanatory form is clear, but the restriction to science-oriented naturalism leaves the range of naturalistic resources partly open.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The demand for such an explanation is stronger than the support shown, although the claim about naturalism is explicitly limited to taking cues from science.

charity.alternative: Naturalism may permit noncausal explanatory resources not yet exemplified in present scientific practice.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce limits his criticism to science-oriented naturalism and says no suitable pattern has been identified, rather than proving impossibility.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference is intelligible, but the bridge from contingency to a required noncausal, nonnecessitating explanation is materially compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The central naturalistic deficit rests substantially on assertion about scientific explanatory patterns and does not compare developed alternatives.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the indispensable pro bridge concerning explanation of the contingent total causal history.

representationalCharity.rationale: The limitation is fairly acknowledged, but the argument still moves quickly from absence of an identified scientific pattern to comparative deficiency.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce argues that history could have differed, demands a noncausal and nonnecessitating explanation, and says science-oriented naturalism lacks an identified pattern.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Creation is appropriately understood as grounding: God's creative activity is a more fundamental reality that unifies and explains the created causal world.
moves.attributionBasis: After the moderator requests clarification, Pearce defines grounding and applies the concept explicitly to God's creative activity.

response.rationale: This constructive move specifies grounding as the proposed relation between divine creative activity and the unified created causal world.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly supplies the subsidiary metaphysical mechanism needed by the preceding contingency argument.

precisionFindings.rationale: Grounding is used consistently as a more-fundamental explanatory relation and its application to creation is readily recoverable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move offers grounding as the appropriate conceptual model rather than claiming that the model independently proves divine creation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The grounding model coherently supplies a noncausal explanatory relation, with only the bridge to actual divine activity left implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Analogical grounding examples support intelligibility, but they do not by themselves verify that divine creation instantiates the relation.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It strongly supports the pro subsidiary grounding bridge by specifying the proposed explanatory relation.

representationalCharity.rationale: The span develops the pro account of creation and does not meaningfully assess a competing account of grounding.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce analogizes familiar grounding relations and describes God's creative activity as the more fundamental reality explaining and unifying creation.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A necessary initial state together with necessary but indeterministic evolution can explain the occurrence of a contingent natural history without an additional non-natural ground.
moves.attributionBasis: The moderator hands the discussion to Graham, who explicitly pushes back and presents the naturalist alternative in the first person.

components.text: Whether contingent history requires an additional noncausal, nonnecessitating divine ground.
Whether divine grounding is needed once a necessary indeterministic natural structure is available.

response.rationale: Oppy directly supplies a rival structure: a necessary initial state and necessary indeterministic evolution yielding a contingent history without an added ground.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it expressly contacts both the alleged naturalistic deficit and the claimed need for divine grounding.

precisionFindings.rationale: The necessary initial state, necessary evolution, indeterminism, and resulting contingent history form a clearly recoverable proposal.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move needs only to establish a coherent naturalistic candidate, and its asserted possibility matches the conceptual construction offered.

charity.alternative: Contingent history requires explanation not merely of its possibility but of why this history occurs.
charity.decisiveQualification: The indeterministic structure explains how a contingent history can arise, while leaving the particular outcome probabilistic rather than necessitated.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The model consistently derives contingent outcomes from necessary indeterministic evolution, with outcome-specific explanation remaining a bounded gap.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual model is clear, but the necessity of the proposed initial state and laws is posited rather than independently defended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supplies the indispensable con natural-history bridge and answers the pro demand for a special ground.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply fairly addresses the demand for nonnecessitation, though it does not fully resolve the stronger demand for outcome-specific explanation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy proposes a necessary initial state with necessary but indeterministic evolution, producing a contingent history without anything further.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Postulating a necessary God does not remove explanatory bruteness unless divine necessity can be explained using resources unavailable to the naturalist.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy begins a direct hypothetical challenge to the necessary-God proposal and contrasts it with his preceding naturalistic account.

components.text: Whether positing necessary divine reality avoids the unexplained starting point charged against naturalism.

response.rationale: Oppy expressly diagnoses an asymmetry: rejecting a necessary natural starting point as unexplained while postulating a necessary God merely relocates the same demand.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it explicitly identifies the disputed asymmetry and states that divine necessity also requires explanatory resources.

precisionFindings.rationale: The conditional challenge is clear: divine necessity removes bruteness only if an asymmetric explanatory resource can be supplied.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The move challenges rather than assumes the impossibility of explaining divine necessity and expressly conditions its conclusion on available resources.

charity.alternative: God's necessity may have an essence-based explanation unavailable to a natural initial state.
charity.decisiveQualification: The reply asks for that asymmetric resource rather than assuming that no such account can possibly be developed.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The symmetry objection is explicit and valid: merely labeling God necessary does not yet answer the demand imposed on a natural starting point.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The dialectical comparison is well supported by the positions stated, though the reply precedes the developed essence-based answer.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con central bridge requiring equal scrutiny of naturalistic and theistic ultimate necessities.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest prospective theistic answer is left open, while the present explanatory symmetry is accurately identified.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy asks what could explain a necessary God's necessity if the natural necessary starting point is rejected for lacking an explanation.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Explanatory inquiry can legitimately terminate in autonomous facts that do not need explanation, with real and nominal definitions providing plausible examples.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce immediately answers Oppy's challenge, adopts an explicit distinction, and develops it through definition-based examples to the context boundary.

components.text: Whether every proposed necessary terminus must face a further explanatory demand.

response.rationale: Pearce answers that explanatory inquiry may properly stop at autonomous facts and identifies real and nominal definitions as plausible stopping points.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the regress demand directly, though the criterion distinguishing autonomous from brute facts remains compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between brute facts needing explanation and autonomous facts for which the question is mistaken is explicitly stated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Definitions are presented as plausible candidates for autonomy rather than conclusively demonstrated exceptionless stopping points.

charity.alternative: Calling a fact autonomous may merely rename unexplained bruteness.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce offers definitions as a principled candidate class where asking for a further explanation may be category-mistaken.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The autonomous-fact distinction coherently answers infinite regress, but its application needs a fuller noncircular criterion.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The cited definitional proposal supplies conceptual support, while the decisive claim that such facts need no explanation remains underdefended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the con symmetric-terminus bridge by proposing a principled category of explanatory stopping point.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply recognizes the regress pressure and offers a criterion, but does not fully show that the criterion is nonstipulative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce distinguishes brute from autonomous facts and follows Gupta in proposing real and nominal definitions as plausible autonomous facts.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: A maximally satisfying ultimate explanation would involve an entity whose real definition or essence entails actual existence, and God is a developed candidate for that role.
moves.attributionBasis: The uninterrupted turn continues Pearce's account of autonomous facts and ends immediately before Oppy's direct naturalistic objection.

response.rationale: This constructive move develops the pro ultimate terminus as an entity whose real essence entails actuality and identifies God as a developed candidate.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it supplies the central essence-based terminus while openly recognizing a possible naturalistic analogue.

precisionFindings.rationale: The ideal terminus and its essence-entails-existence condition are clear, and God's status is qualified as a traditional candidate.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce explicitly calls the naturalistic version possible but personally less plausible, avoiding a claim of demonstrated theistic uniqueness.

charity.alternative: A naturalist could assign essence-entailing existence to fundamental natural entities.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce explicitly acknowledges that proposal while judging God the more developed and plausible candidate.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The essence-based terminus is coherent as a proposed stopping point, but the inference from definition or essence to actuality remains compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: God is identified through a philosophical tradition, but comparative support for divine over natural essence is largely asserted.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supplies the pro central bridge seeking a principled ultimate terminus whose essence entails existence.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest naturalistic analogue is stated rather than suppressed, although the basis for finding it less plausible is not developed here.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce says complete explanation without bruteness would involve essence entailing actual existence and acknowledges both natural and divine candidates.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A naturalist can nominate the universe's initial state as an entity whose essence includes existence, so that explanatory structure does not uniquely favor theism.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy explicitly enters with a brief objection, and Pearce begins his answer in the following source row.

components.text: Whether essence-entailing existence provides a comparative resource unique to theism.

response.rationale: Oppy directly accepts the proposed explanatory form for argument's sake and nominates the universe's initial state as a naturalistic instance.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it expressly contacts the claimed comparative asymmetry and supplies the precise rival candidate the argument must exclude.

precisionFindings.rationale: The conditional naturalistic proposal is concise, stable, and explicitly depends on accepting Pearce's account of real definition.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The reply establishes a candidate rather than asserting that the initial state's essence has independently been proven to entail existence.

charity.alternative: God has a uniquely developed essence-based necessity unavailable to a natural initial state.
charity.decisiveQualification: The reply does not deny theological development; it argues that the explanatory schema itself permits a parallel natural candidate.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Given the shared essence-based framework, the inference to lack of unique theistic advantage is clear, with candidate adequacy left open.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The symmetry point is supported, but the actual essence and necessary existence of the initial state are nominated rather than defended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con symmetric-terminus bridge by applying equal explanatory scrutiny and resources to naturalism.

representationalCharity.rationale: It accurately targets uniqueness without pretending that merely nominating the natural candidate establishes its ultimate metaphysics.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy says a naturalist accepting real definitions can nominate the universe's initial state as the entity whose essence includes existence.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Default trust in human cognitive faculties and testimony extends presumptively to the widespread practice of interpreting experiences as encounters with God or supernatural reality.
moves.attributionBasis: After the moderated topic transition, Pearce presents the religious-experience case continuously until Oppy asks what qualifies as such an experience.

response.rationale: This constructive move extends a general presumptive trust in cognition and testimony to widespread practices of interpreting religious experience.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it gives a clear epistemic principle and application, though calibration conditions are not yet adequately specified.

precisionFindings.rationale: The default-trust claim is clear, but the boundaries of religious experience and the relevant faculty or practice remain partly unsettled.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Extending ordinary presumptive trust to supernatural interpretation requires calibration qualifications that are only implicit in this span.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The extension is intelligible, but the bridge from trust in faculties generally to trust in supernatural interpretations remains material.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Widespread practice and analogy with testimony provide support, but reliability, independence, and alternative-cause comparisons are not defended.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the pro central religious-experience bridge by supplying a presumptive evidential principle.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move principally develops its own epistemic extension and does not yet engage a specific calibrated naturalistic alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce cites widespread ordinary and extraordinary religious interpretation and argues that default trust should extend to this human practice.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: A broad category of religious experience is readily explained naturalistically, while a narrower evidentially stronger category raises doubts about how frequently such experiences occur.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy poses a sustained definitional dilemma with personal and testimonial examples, ending when Pearce begins his analogy with arguments from evil.

components.text: Whether the relevant class of religious experiences is both common and evidentially strong.

response.rationale: Oppy diagnoses a scope dilemma: breadth supports prevalence but weakens evidential distinctiveness, while a narrow stronger class loses the prevalence premise.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within diagnostic defeats, it explicitly identifies the unstable comparison class and states the consequence for the default-trust inference.

precisionFindings.rationale: The two horns are clearly separated according to breadth, evidential strength, and frequency of the relevant experience class.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy requests specification and raises a conditional dilemma rather than claiming that every religious experience is naturally explained.

charity.alternative: A broad category may contain experiences of varying quality that deserve different evidential weights.
charity.decisiveQualification: The objection asks for precisely that differentiation because breadth alone cannot establish the prevalence of stronger cases.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The breadth-frequency tradeoff is a clear dilemma, though a continuous quality-weighted account could avoid an exhaustive binary.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual challenge is strong, but claims about natural explanation and actual frequency are not supported with representative empirical evidence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the pro central religious-experience bridge by challenging both prevalence and evidential calibration.

representationalCharity.rationale: The strongest quality-sensitive interpretation remains available, and the reply accurately identifies the calibration work it must perform.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts a common broad category readily treated naturalistically with a narrower stronger category whose actual frequency requires support.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Religious experience should be construed broadly and weighted by quality, while its first-person character can justify an experiencer's non-neutral stance despite disagreement.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce directly answers Oppy's classificatory challenge through an extended analogy and epistemic account, ending before Oppy's next objection.

components.text: How breadth, quality, and frequency should determine the evidential weight of religious experience.

response.rationale: Pearce replaces a binary broad-versus-narrow classification with graded quality weighting and explains why first-person access changes personal justification.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within justified reframes, it preserves the calibration issue and answers it with graded weighting, though population-level force remains incomplete.

precisionFindings.rationale: The graded proposal is clear, but the scope of first-person justification and its relation to public comparative evidence remains partly open.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce claims differential personal justification rather than uniform reliability, explicitly distinguishing ordinary from extraordinary cases.

charity.alternative: Broad religious experience may be common only because it includes weak and naturally expected cases.
charity.decisiveQualification: Pearce accepts quality differences and assigns different weights instead of treating every broad-category case as equally probative.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Graded weighting avoids the binary dilemma, but the bridge from first-person justification to worldview comparison remains partly implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The experiential epistemology is plausible, while reliability conditions and evidence for the distribution of high-quality cases remain compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the con experience-calibration bridge by offering a quality-sensitive alternative to its dilemma.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection's strongest calibration concern is retained, although the answer does not quantify how much weight stronger cases deserve.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce construes religious experience broadly, distinguishes extraordinary quality, and argues that first-person access affects the experiencer's justification.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: Human faculties are not trusted without qualification; experience teaches the circumstances in which each faculty is unreliable.
moves.attributionBasis: The turn directly follows Pearce's account and is explicitly framed as a response to his claim about general trust.

components.text: Whether general trust in human faculties can remain unqualified when applied to religious interpretation.
Whether first-person experience must still be assessed under learned conditions of faculty unreliability.

response.rationale: Oppy directly rejects unqualified general trust and substitutes developmentally learned, circumstance-sensitive calibration for every faculty.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it expressly contacts the default-trust premise and also bears directly on the later quality-sensitive proposal.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is explicitly universal across faculties but limited to the need for circumstance-sensitive trust rather than global distrust.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The familiar developmental claim that trust is circumstance-sensitive is proportionate and does not overstate which religious cases fail.

charity.alternative: Default trust can be defeasible and therefore already compatible with later calibration.
charity.decisiveQualification: Oppy argues that learned calibration is constitutive of warranted trust, not merely an optional exception added afterward.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference from known circumstance-sensitive unreliability to calibrated rather than blanket faculty trust is clear and consistent.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Ordinary developmental experience supports the general point, but no religiously specific reliability conditions or mechanisms are supplied here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the con central experience-calibration bridge by stating the governing epistemic requirement.

representationalCharity.rationale: The defeasible interpretation is implicitly accommodated, though the reply somewhat compresses the difference between default and unqualified trust.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy says people learn when faculties cannot be trusted and that this circumstance-sensitive self-understanding applies across faculties.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: The disorder and ambiguity of religious experience fit nonintentional causes better than communication from an agent intending relationship with human beings.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy develops an explicit disanalogy between inquiry into nonintentional objects and interaction with an intentional communicating agent.

components.text: Whether ambiguous and divergent experiences fit an intentional divine source as well as nonintentional causes.

response.rationale: Oppy directly contrasts inquiry into nonintentional entities with communication by an agent who supposedly intends relationship, deriving different expectations.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the explanatory-fit issue, though it does not exhaust possible divine purposes for ambiguity.

precisionFindings.rationale: The agent-versus-nonagent contrast is clear, while the particular divine communicative intention is a material but reasonably recoverable assumption.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Disorder plausibly favors nonintentional causes, but the strength depends on an only implicitly specified divine purpose and expected clarity.

charity.alternative: A relational God may permit ambiguity for purposes other than transmitting uniform propositional information.
charity.decisiveQualification: The objection concerns an agent intending relationship, for whom severe persistent communicative disorder still requires an account.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The expectation contrast is coherent, but the inference requires a substantive premise about what successful divine relationship would communicate.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Observed ambiguity is relevant, while the comparative likelihood under divine intentions versus natural causes is not systematically established.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con central religious-disorder bridge by linking ambiguity to expectations of intentional communication.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move targets a plausible relational expectation but leaves broader divine-purpose alternatives underdeveloped.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts difficult investigation of nonintentional objects with an intentional agent who is supposedly trying to communicate and relate.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: Religious experience need not primarily aim at uniform detailed theology and should instead be assessed through whole traditions, lived effects, testimony, and long-term communal functioning.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce identifies the objection as a hiddenness puzzle, rejects a specific divine aim, and then gives his alternative method of evaluation.

components.text: What successful divine communication should be expected to accomplish across religious traditions.

response.rationale: Pearce rejects uniform detailed theology as the assumed divine aim and proposes holistic assessment through traditions, testimony, effects, and communal life.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within justified reframes, it challenges and replaces the communicative criterion, but supplies only limited support for the alternative divine purpose.

precisionFindings.rationale: The rejected uniform-theology aim is clear, but the proposed holistic purpose and standards of successful functioning remain loosely specified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce explicitly concedes that disorder may remain a problem for other views while denying the strongest assumed communicative objective.

charity.alternative: Intentional divine relationship should produce substantially clearer and less disordered communication.
charity.decisiveQualification: That expectation is strongest if uniform detailed theology is the primary aim; other relational aims may be assessed holistically.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Rejecting a single informational aim is coherent, but the replacement criterion needs a fuller bridge from holistic effects to divine communication.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The alternative purpose is plausible but largely speculative, with no representative comparison of traditions, effects, or naturalistic rivals.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the con central religious-disorder bridge by disputing its assumed criterion of communicative success.

representationalCharity.rationale: Pearce preserves the hiddenness concern and explicitly says it may remain, while narrowing the expectation he rejects.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce denies that uniform detailed theology exhausts divine purposes and proposes judging whole traditions through testimony, effects, and communal functioning.

moves.speaker: Graham Oppy
moves.proposition: The enduring diversity of radically different religious traditions resists a plausible single-religion account and is easier for naturalism to explain.
moves.attributionBasis: Oppy introduces the Rainbow Serpent tradition, compares it with several major religions, and explicitly draws the comparative naturalist conclusion.

components.text: Whether radically different enduring traditions admit a plausible unified theistic account under holistic assessment.

response.rationale: Oppy directly tests the holistic response against sharply different traditions and argues that their diversity is easier to unify naturalistically.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the replacement holistic criterion with a concrete diversity case and comparative conclusion.

precisionFindings.rationale: The comparative claim is explicitly framed as naturalism having an easier explanatory task, not as logical incompatibility with theism.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Oppy's stated inability to see a plausible unifying single-religion story appropriately qualifies the comparative conclusion.

charity.alternative: Different traditions may interpret genuine divine encounters through distinct inherited conceptual frameworks.
charity.decisiveQualification: The greater the enduring doctrinal and experiential divergence, the more substantive the needed unifying theistic interpretation becomes.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The comparative inference from radical durable diversity to easier naturalistic explanation is coherent, though not deductively decisive.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Several contrasting traditions provide concrete support, but representativeness and comparative likelihoods are not developed in depth.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the con central religious-disorder bridge through a comparative explanation of enduring diversity.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move leaves reinterpretation logically open but reasonably presses the explanatory cost imposed by the scale of diversity.

moves.evidenceBasis: Oppy contrasts the Rainbow Serpent tradition with Christianity, Hinduism, and Buddhism and says naturalism more easily explains their divergence.

moves.speaker: Kenny Pearce
moves.proposition: A long-isolated religious tradition may reflect genuine experiences of God interpreted through its inherited framework rather than faculties wholly disconnected from reality.
moves.attributionBasis: Pearce acknowledges limited knowledge of the example, discusses the anthropological uncertainty, and formulates the competing theistic interpretation himself.

components.text: Whether a long-isolated divergent tradition must count as evidence of faculties disconnected from divine reality.

response.rationale: Pearce directly offers a competing interpretation in which genuine experiences of God are rendered through an inherited cultural framework.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it contacts the concrete diversity example, but its acknowledged limited knowledge makes the proposed interpretation tentative.

precisionFindings.rationale: The alternative interpretation is recoverable, but its application to the particular tradition is explicitly tentative and anthropologically underdetermined.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Pearce presents a possible theistic interpretation and openly acknowledges limited knowledge rather than asserting that it is established.

charity.alternative: The isolated tradition's divergence is better explained by culturally generated faculties and natural social inheritance.
charity.decisiveQualification: Cultural mediation alone does not show that the underlying experiences are wholly disconnected from reality.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Cultural interpretation of genuine experience is coherent, but the inference offers compatibility more clearly than comparative explanation.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The proposed reading is speculative and explicitly rests on limited knowledge, without independent evidence distinguishing it from the naturalistic account.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the con central religious-disorder bridge, though chiefly by preserving a live alternative interpretation.

representationalCharity.rationale: The naturalistic interpretation is accurately retained as a live option while Pearce identifies a genuine underdetermination in the example.

moves.evidenceBasis: Pearce acknowledges uncertainty about the example and suggests genuine experiences of God may be interpreted through an inherited isolated framework.
